routes.title: /pdf-viewer vs /docs/components/pdf-viewer

state.note: Both sides use the upstream default chrome: the thumbnails sidebar is closed, there is no optional status bar, and the viewer copy is English. Zoom is pinned to 1 on both sides; the upstream docs demo defaults to 0.5.

gate.reason: The page bitmap is produced by the product's pinned EmbedPDF 2.14.4 while the reference runs 2.15.0, so its rasterisation is an environment difference (differences.page-raster-renderer-version). The blocking gate covers the product shell (chrome-only pixels), the geometry landmarks and console errors; full-page pixels stay in the report as a diagnostic. See docs/testing/ui-parity-routes.md sections 6 and 8.

reference.readyFunction: () => { const img = document.querySelector('[data-slot="pdf-viewer"] [data-pdf-viewer-page="1"] img'); return !!img && img.complete && img.naturalWidth > 0; }

prepare.reason: The demo nav and page scaffolding are excluded from the product region. Hide them before capture so the region sits in the same 24px + 1px host shell as the reference route (viewer top 25px, inside the viewport) instead of far below the demo controls, where Chromium rasterises offscreen content with a different SVG antialiasing phase.
prepare.script: () => { const nav = document.querySelector('.nav'); if (nav) nav.style.display = 'none'; const page = document.querySelector('[data-testid="pdf-viewer-page"]'); if (!page) return; for (const child of [...page.children]) { if (!child.classList.contains('viewer-container')) child.style.display = 'none'; } }

prepare.reason: The demo page's text metrics can leave the viewer on a fractional CSS pixel at some widths. Add the remainder to the page's top padding so the product region starts on an integer CSS pixel. This is capture scaffolding, not a product change.
prepare.script: () => { const region = document.querySelector('[data-testid="pdf-viewer"]'); const page = document.querySelector('[data-testid="pdf-viewer-page"]'); if (!region || !page) return; const top = region.getBoundingClientRect().top; const fraction = top - Math.floor(top); if (fraction > 0.001) { const padding = Number.parseFloat(getComputedStyle(page).paddingTop) || 0; page.style.paddingTop = `${padding + 1 - fraction}px`; } }

defaults.source: packages/vue-pdf/src/components/PdfViewer.vue:121 `showThumbnails = ref(false)` matches upstream pdf-viewer.tsx:2281 `useState(false)`; apps/demo/src/lib/route-capture.ts:44 keeps the opt-in status bar off unless `?statusbar=on` is passed. No prepare click is needed.

region.widthRule: 100% of the page content box: 24px page padding + 1200px max width + 1px region frame, reproduced identically on both sides

exclusions.reason: The docs page renders a usage code block under the preview; the product region ends at [data-slot="pdf-viewer"].
Docs preview card (rounded border, page margins) wraps the product component; the harness reproduces only its box metrics so both regions receive the same width.
Demo-only page header, sample selector, runtime-policy panel, status grid and diagnostics list; the upstream docs page has none of them.

Global demo navigation above the page. The capture hides it so the product region sits in the reference host shell (24px page padding + 1px frame) instead of below a sticky nav; it is never part of the region.
Demo frame (1px border, radius, overflow) that wraps the viewer; only its box metrics are reproduced on the reference side.

differences.impact: The shipped route starts without the 160px thumbnail sidebar; the toolbar toggle still opens and closes it.

differences.evidence: packages/vue-pdf/src/components/PdfViewer.vue:93 keeps `showStatusBar: false`; apps/demo/src/lib/route-capture.ts:44 now makes the demo status bar opt-in (`?statusbar=on`) instead of on by default.
differences.impact: The default route no longer renders `pdf-status-bar`, matching the upstream viewer. Hosts can still opt in through the existing `showStatusBar` prop.

differences.evidence: packages/vue-pdf/src/components/PdfViewer.vue:2013 paints `color-mix(in oklab, var(--office-muted) 30%, var(--office-background))`, the `bg-muted/30` equivalent from upstream apps/v4/components/extend/pdf-viewer.tsx:580; rendered light #fcfcfc, dark #0d0d0d.
differences.impact: The page canvas now uses the same muted-over-background surface as the reference in both themes.

differences.evidence: packages/vue-pdf/src/components/PdfViewer.vue:2037 defaults the dark page filter to the same 0.35px softening as light mode; only an explicit `--pdf-dark-page-filter` opt-in can add a transform.
differences.impact: Dark-mode page content keeps its original colours, like the upstream viewer.
Page glyph edges soften like the reference; CSS filters do not change the image box, so the page geometry landmarks are unchanged.

differences.evidence: packages/vue-pdf/src/components/PdfViewer.vue:2129 keeps only `.pdf-body { flex-direction: column }` at container width <= 760px; `.pdf-frame-wrap` keeps its 24px padding at every width, matching upstream `PAGE_GAP = 24` (pdf-viewer.tsx:172,2924).
differences.impact: The page frame no longer shifts by 12px at 768/390; the page1 landmark delta is inside its 1px tolerance.

differences.evidence: Reference page frame is 595.266 x 841.875 CSS px, ours 595 x 841.281 (capture report `geometry.landmarks.page1`).
differences.impact: Sub-pixel rounding of the zoom-1 page size; contributes to raster diff but stays under the 1px landmark budget.

differences.evidence: packages/vue-pdf/package.json pins `@embedpdf/*@2.14.4`; the reference app uses `@embedpdf/*@2.15.0` (tools/extend-reference/package.json).
differences.impact: The page bitmap rasterisation (text hinting, tiling, page-size rounding) can differ even when both sides paint the same PDF bytes. This is why the blocking route gate covers chrome-only pixels plus geometry, and keeps full-page pixels as a diagnostic.

notes: Pilot route for #182: proves an upstream pinned wrapper can be rendered verbatim (R2) and compared region-to-region.

#199 fixed the six classified product deltas and flipped gateStatus to `blocking`: chrome-only pixels, landmarks and console errors gate; full-page raster pixels stay diagnostic because the renderer version differs.
